This axon's centres scatter off a smooth outline by about 81 nm (4% of its radius, estimated from its own centres, so rough), and a healthy ring that scatters that much stays under 691 nm 99 times in 100. 1 of them is deeper than that too: it is probably not on the membrane, or the axon is more concave than any simulated shape. Raised to 16,484 samples to keep the sub-nanometre spacing the method specifies. | KS p-value compares 50 experimental distances against 50,000 pooled randomized ones, with such an unbalanced sample size almost any difference reaches significance. Contour drawn by hand along the membrane.

44 of the 53 cluster centres sit more than 60 nm from the path drawn along the membrane (the furthest by 1350 nm). The contour still passes through them, so each pulls it off the path; if they are not on the membrane, the axoplasm panel is where they are discarded.

1 of the 53 centres on this contour sit more than 767 nm inside their own convex hull, the deepest by 1,387 nm: deeper than any simulated ring whose centres scatter off the outline by up to 5 % of its radius reaches, with gaps, dents or a waist a third of its width. This axon's centres scatter off a smooth outline by about 92 nm (5% of its radius, estimated from its own centres, so rough), and a healthy ring that scatters that much stays under 727 nm 99 times in 100. 1 of them is deeper than that too: it is probably not on the membrane, or the axon is more concave than any simulated shape. Look at the contour before using the perimeter: it is 1.31 times the hull of the same centres (12.69 um), and clusters per um, occupancy and the randomization all follow it.
Perimeter is 16.7 um, so 10,000 samples would sit 1.67 nm apart. Raised to 16,657 samples to keep the sub-nanometre spacing the method specifies.

KS p-value compares 53 experimental distances against 53,000 pooled randomized ones; with such an unbalanced sample size almost any difference reaches significance. Interpret D = 0.122 and the CDF shapes, not the p-value alone.
